Hence the Lean `chamber` is literally "connected component of 𝓤_n/(ℤ/n) with the quotient topology" — the printed def:chamber (sm-1-polygons.tex:206-211), neither larger nor smaller. (Also: quotienting the open σ-saturated 𝓤_n directly vs. taking the generic part of (ℝ²)^n/(ℤ/n) gives the same topology, since a finite-group quotient map is open and its restriction to an open saturated set is an open surjection, hence a quotient map — so no alternative reading of 𝓤_n/(ℤ/n) changes the components.)

ATTACK 1 — "quantifying over labelled representatives asserts MORE than constancy on quotient chambers." Fails. C = cornerStateSum hn hP is defined on labelled tuples (CornerStateSum.lean:166), so for a function f on 𝓤_n and a chamber K ⊆ 𝓤_n/(ℤ/n), "f is constant on K" can only mean f is constant on π⁻¹(K). The field (statement file lines 21-23) says ∀ P Q, π Q ∈ connectedComponent(π P) → C P = C Q, i.e. exactly "∀ K, C constant on π⁻¹(K)" (every K is connectedComponent(π P) for some P by Quotient.exists_rep). The field entails cyclic invariance (take Q = shift k P: π Q = π P ∈ chamber(π P), so C P = C (shift k P)); but that is not unprinted content — it is what the printed sentence needs to be meaningful given def:chamber, and the printed proof asserts and uses it explicitly ("cyclically shifting the vertex labels preserves C directly from its definition ... makes it descend", sm-4-knotlaws.tex:87-98). So there is no configuration where Lean demands an equality the printed statement does not.

ATTACK 2 — "two labelled polygons in different labelled chambers but the same quotient chamber are missed." Fails. The hypothesis is membership of π Q in the QUOTIENT component of π P, not Q ∈ connectedComponent P in GenericTuple. Concretely, if P and Q lie in distinct labelled components L, L' with L' = σ^k(L) (so π(L)=π(L') and π Q ∈ chamber(π P)), the field applies and forces C P = C Q. Conversely nothing extra is demanded: for a finite group acting by homeomorphisms π is open and closed, so for a labelled component L ⊆ π⁻¹(K) the saturated set ∪_k σ^k L has open-and-closed image inside connected K, hence π⁻¹(K) = ∪_k σ^k L exactly — which is the printed parenthetical of def:chamber ("a union of at most n components permuted by σ"). Therefore the field is provably equivalent to [cyclic invariance] ∧ [constancy on each labelled chamber], which is precisely what the printed proof establishes (lines 41-85 labelled path; 87-98 descent). Equivalent in both directions: neither STRONGER nor WEAKER.

ATTACK 3 — "Lean chamber notion larger/smaller than printed." Fails as shown in SETUP: same space, same group (exactly ℤ/n via shift, not dihedral; orbit relation is direction-independent so σ-convention is irrelevant), same quotient topology, same connectedComponent.

DOMAIN. ∀ n [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n): n ≥ 3 matches the printed polygon convention (Polygon takes _hn : 3 ≤ n, Polygon.lean:47).
